dedupe_keys.name: sagis south african grain information weekly producer deliveries and imports and exports and monthly supply and demand stocks deliveries consumption feed exports of maize wheat oilseeds and other grains

description: SAGIS is the industry body that collects and publishes official information on South Africa's grain and oilseed markets, under statutory reporting by all grain handlers. Its weekly data give producer deliveries of maize, by grade, wheat, soybeans and sunflower for each marketing season since the mid 2000s, and weekly imports and exports of maize and wheat, with declared intentions to trade eight weeks ahead. Its monthly data give full supply and demand balances for each grain, including maize, wheat, sorghum, sunflower, soybeans, groundnuts, canola, oats and barley: opening stocks, deliveries from farms, imports, use for human consumption, animal feed and biofuel, seed, exports and closing stocks, in English, Tswana and Zulu. Coverage is national. The files are free and available to download as Excel from the SAGIS site; no licence terms are stated. Caveats: weekly deliveries are unverified and revised, stocks are reported by handlers, not by storage site, and file layouts differ between seasons. Simulation uses: tracking national grain stocks and flows to test food supply resilience to drought or port disruption, and calibrating supply chain models for southern Africa, which depends on South African maize. Related records: the IGC grain market report (data-igc-grain-market-report-supply-demand) gives global balances, and the USDA export grain inspections (data-usda-fgis-export-grain-inspections) are a comparable national trade series.
